transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you in to see me?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate you taking the time. 

Um, I guess I came in because... well, it's probably nothing too serious, just a little communication hiccup, really. I'm an artist, and lately I've been getting some feedback that my artist statements and my client notes are a little... hard to follow? 

People keep telling me they don't really understand what I'm trying to explain. Like, in meetings, I guess I start jumping around a lot. I'll go from talking about, you know, the physical textures of a piece, straight into the budgets, and then... well, sometimes I get really into the, um, the secret meanings behind the work. Which I guess throws people off. 

I'm probably just being a little too scattered, right? I just really don't want to make a bad impression on my clients or seem unprofessional, so I thought it would be best to come talk to someone. Is that an okay reason to be here? I hope I'm explaining this right.
Could you tell me more about what you mean by the secret meanings behind your work?

Oh, um... well, it's a little embarrassing to explain, actually. I really don't want you to think I'm being, you know, totally unreasonable or anything. 

It's just... sometimes, I'll notice these little details. Like a very specific stain on a canvas, or the way a seam is sewn, or... or even just a certain phrase in an email from a gallery. And I get this really strong conviction that it's a message meant specifically for me? Like it's a hidden instruction, or maybe a warning about what I need to do with a piece. 

I know it probably sounds a bit silly when I say it out loud. And usually, a friend or a colleague will point out a perfectly ordinary explanation, like, "Oh, it's just a generic mass email," or "It's just a watermark," but... I find it really, really hard to let go of that feeling. Even when they show me the completely logical answer, I just can't shake it. 

It's probably just my artist brain working in overdrive, right? Is that... is that something you've heard before from creative types? I really hope I'm not coming across as too strange.
Have you ever had experiences where you heard sounds or voices that other people couldn't hear?

Um... well... I guess, maybe a little bit? But it's really nothing major, I promise. It's probably just because I spend so much time alone in the studio, you know? When it's really quiet, your mind can sort of play tricks on you.

Sometimes, when I'm working by myself, I'll hear... like, a woman's voice? Just very quietly commenting on things, coming from behind the supply shelves. Or, um, occasionally I'll get this really strong smell of hot metal near a piece I haven't finished yet. 

And in the moment, it feels completely, one hundred percent real. But then I'll go check behind the shelves, or look for a short circuit, and... there's absolutely nothing there. 

It's just stress and being tired, right? Like, sensory overload from focusing too hard? I really try not to let it bother me, and I definitely don't let it interfere with my deadlines. I hope that doesn't make me sound too crazy... is that something that happens to people when they're just overworked?
About how long have you been noticing these experiences, like the hidden messages and the sounds?

Um, let's see... I guess it's been going on for a little while now. Maybe around... 11 months? Roughly? 

I know that sounds like a long time, but it really hasn't been a big deal, I promise. It's just been sort of... hovering in the background while I work. The messages and the voice, and sometimes the smells... they just started popping up around then. 

But I've been keeping up with all my commissions, and I've been doing my best to just push through it and stay professional. I really hope I haven't let it get too out of hand before coming in. Is 11 months... is that a really bad amount of time to wait before talking to someone? I just wanted to make sure I wasn't wasting your time with something minor.
Over these past 11 months, have you had periods where you felt persistently sad, depressed, or empty for weeks at a time?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I definitely have days where I feel a little unmotivated or tired, but I think that's just normal, right? Like, everyone gets a bit down sometimes, especially when a project isn't going well or the weather is bad. 

But I definitely haven't felt empty or, you know, deeply depressed for weeks at a time. I always manage to pull myself together and get back to the studio. I try really hard to stay positive and keep moving forward. I wouldn't want to let a bad mood ruin my productivity, you know? 

So, yeah, nothing like that. I hope that's a good thing? It means I'm coping okay in that department, at least, right?
